chunks: 2138 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said:
I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام speaking to the people in Makkah. He said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله prayed Fajr with his companions, then sat with them speaking to them until the sun rose. Then one man after another began to stand and leave, until none remained with him except two men: an Anṣārī and a Thaqafī.

So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to them: 'I know that you both have a matter you wish to ask me about. If you wish, I shall inform you of your need before you ask me, and if you wish, then ask me.' They said: 'Rather, you inform us, O Messenger of Allah, for that is clearer for blindness, farther from doubt, and firmer for faith.'

Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'As for you, O brother of the Anṣār, you are from a people who “prefer others over themselves,” and you are a townsman while this Thaqafī is a Bedouin. Will you prefer him in asking the question?' He said: 'Yes.'

He said: 'As for you, O brother of Thaqīf, you came to ask me about your wudu (ablution) and your salat (prayer), and what belongs to you in them. So know that when you put your hand into the water and say, “In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful,” the sins your hands earned scatter away. Then when you wash your face, the sins your eyes earned by their looking, and your mouth by its speech, scatter away.'

Then when you wash your forearms, the sins scatter away from your right and your left. Then when you wipe your head and your feet, the sins you walked toward on your feet scatter away. This is for you in your wudu (ablution).'

Then when you stand for salat (prayer), turn yourself, recite Umm al-Kitāb and whatever is easy for you of the surahs, then bow and complete its bowing and its prostration, and recite the tashahhud and give salām, every sin between you and the salat (prayer) that preceded it up to the later salat (prayer) is forgiven for you.

This is for you in your salat (prayer). As for you, O brother of the Anṣār, you came to ask me about your hajj and your ʿumrah, and what reward is for you in them. So know that when you set out upon the way of hajj, then mount your riding beast and say: “In the Name of Allah,” and your riding beast proceeds with you, it does not place a hoof nor lift a hoof except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes for you a good deed and erases from you a sin.

Then when you enter iḥrām and recite the talbiyah, Allah, Exalted is He, writes for you ten good deeds in every talbiyah and erases from you ten sins. Then when you circumambulate the House for seven rounds, by that there is for you with Allah a covenant and remembrance; your Lord is shy before you to punish you after it.

Then when you pray two rakʿahs at the Maqām, Allah writes for you by them two thousand accepted rakʿahs. And when you perform saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah for seven circuits, there is for you by that with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the like of the reward of one who performed hajj walking from his land, and the like of the reward of one who freed seventy believing slaves.

And when you stand at ʿArafāt until sunset, then even if upon you were sins like the sand of ʿĀlij and the foam of the sea, Allah would surely forgive them for you. Then when you cast the pebbles at the jamarāt, Allah writes for you with every pebble ten good deeds in what remains ahead of your life.

Then when you shave your head, there is for you, by the number of every hair, a good deed written for you in what remains ahead of your life. Then when you slaughter your sacrificial offering or sacrifice your camel, there is for you, with every drop of its blood, a good deed written for you in what remains ahead of your life.

Then when you circumambulate the House for seven rounds for the visitation and pray two rakʿahs at the Maqām, a noble angel strikes upon your shoulders and says: 'As for what has passed, it has surely been forgiven for you, so begin the deeds anew for what is between you and one hundred and twenty days.'

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: the talbiyah recited in iḥrām, for which repeated reward is written
key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: the jamarāt, the stoning rite during hajj for which reward is granted
key_terms.الْمَقَامِ: the Maqām, the station where two rakʿahs are prayed after tawāf
key_terms.حَجِّكَ: your hajj, the pilgrimage whose rites carry immense reward
key_terms.صَلَاتِكَ: your salat (prayer), whose proper performance brings forgiveness
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: ʿArafāt, the place of standing in hajj where sins are forgiven
key_terms.عُمْرَتِكَ: your ʿumrah, the lesser pilgrimage mentioned alongside hajj
key_terms.وُضُوئِكَ: your wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What rewards does this hadith mention for wudu, salat, hajj, and ʿumrah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the spiritual rewards and forgiveness associated with wudu (ablution), salat (prayer), hajj, and ʿumrah, as taught by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. It also highlights the virtue of the Anṣār in preferring others over themselves and presents a detailed prophetic explanation of how acts of worship erase sins and increase reward.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2138 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:
I heard Abu Ja’far (as) narrating to the people in Makkah. Imam (as) said:

"The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, prayed Fajr with his companions and then sat with them, speaking to them until the sun rose. One by one, the men began to leave until only two remained: one Ansari and one Thaqafi.

The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said to them: 'I know that you both have a need you wish to ask me about. If you wish, I can inform you of your needs before you ask, or if you wish, you may ask me directly.'
They said: 'You inform us, O Messenger of Allah (swt), for that is clearer for our hearts, removes doubt, and strengthens our faith.'

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said: 'As for you, O brother from the Ansar, you are from a people who "prefer others over themselves" (Surah Al-Hashr, 59:9). You are a city-dweller, and this Thaqafi is a Bedouin. Would you prefer to let him ask first?'
He replied: 'Yes.'

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said: 'As for you, O brother from Thaqif, you came to ask me about your ablution and prayer and what reward you gain from them. Know that when you strike your hands into the water and say, "In the name of Allah (swt), the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," the sins committed by your hands fall away. When you wash your face, the sins committed by your eyes from what they looked at, and by your mouth from what it uttered, also fall away

When you wash your arms, the sins fall away from your right and left sides. When you wipe your head and feet, the sins you walked toward with your feet fall away. This is the reward for your ablution.

When you stand for prayer, direct yourself toward Allah (swt), recite the Opening Chapter of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha) and whatever is easy for you of other chapters, then bow and complete your bowing, prostrate and complete your prostration, recite the testimony (Tashahhud), and say the salutations (Tasleem), all the sins committed between the earlier prayer and the one you just performed are forgiven. This is the reward for your prayer.

As for you, O brother from the Ansar, you came to ask me about your Hajj and Umrah and the reward you gain from them. Know that when you set out on the path of Hajj, mount your riding animal, and say, "In the name of Allah (swt)," each time your riding animal places its hoof down and lifts it, Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, writes a good deed for you and erases a sin from you.

When you enter Ihram and say the Talbiyah (Labbaik Allahumma Labbaik), Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, writes ten good deeds for you with every Talbiyah and erases ten sins from you. When you circumambulate the House seven times, you are given a covenant and a remembrance from Allah (swt). Your Lord (azj) feels shy to punish you after that.

When you pray two units of prayer (Rak’ahs) at the Station of Ibrahim, Allah (swt) writes for you the reward of two thousand accepted prayers. When you walk seven circuits between Safa and Marwah, you are granted a reward from Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, equivalent to that of someone who performed Hajj on foot from their homeland and the reward of someone who freed seventy believing slaves.

When you stand at Arafat until sunset, even if your sins were as numerous as the grains of sand in Alij or the foam of the sea, Allah (swt) forgives them for you. When you cast the pebbles at the Jamarat, Allah (swt) writes ten good deeds for each pebble for the rest of your life.

When you shave your head, for each hair that is removed, a good deed is written for you for the remainder of your life. When you sacrifice your offering or slaughter your animal, for every drop of its blood, a good deed is written for you for the rest of your life.

When you circumambulate the Kaaba seven times as part of the visitation (Tawaf al-Ziyarah) and pray two units of prayer at the Station of Ibrahim, a noble angel strikes your shoulders and says, 'As for what has passed, it has been forgiven for you, so start anew with good deeds for the next 120 days.'
